sections.h2: Who records deeds in Antrim County, and what does the office hold?
sections.html:
The Antrim County Register of Deeds records every deed, mortgage and lien that touches land in the county, and the office sits in the county administration building at Bellaire. Staff keep a grantor and grantee index, and the register also chairs the County Plat Board that reviews new subdivisions. The office posts weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The records run deep. Antrim County's own page says its filings date back to 1856, with computer images from January 1990 forward and older material in book form. The statutory name index from the start of the county to the present can be searched free of charge at the public terminal, and the office asks visitors to book an appointment for that terminal.

Michigan follows a race-notice rule, and the register's page spells out what that means for a seller: once a deed is recorded, later buyers are treated as having notice of it. That is why the office date-stamps and numbers every document in the order it arrives. If you are closing on a lake house in Antrim County, the title company will normally send the deed to the office the same day it funds.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Antrim County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed in Antrim County costs a flat $30.00 per document, no matter how many pages it runs. Extra charges apply only in a few situations, listed here from the county fee schedule.

  • A document that assigns or discharges more than one instrument adds $3.00 for each extra instrument.
  • A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, or a land contract (or an assignment or amendment that changes the legal description) needs a tax certificate from the County Treasurer for $5.00.
  • Copies of recorded documents are $1.00 per page, plat copies are $2.00 per page, and certifying a copy is $5.00 for the first page.

Payment can be made by check, cash or credit card, and checks should be made out to the Antrim County Register of Deeds. The $5.00 tax certificate is a separate item that goes through the treasurer.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured when an Antrim County house sells?
sections.html:
Transfer tax is charged on the sale price in blocks of $500, and the register's office collects it when the deed is recorded. Other Michigan register offices post a combined rate of $4.30 per $500, made up of $3.75 for the state and $0.55 for the county, and the figure is rounded up for any partial block. Ask the Antrim office to confirm the county portion before you budget.

The Census Bureau lists the median value of owner-occupied homes in Antrim County at $255,500 for 2020 to 2024. A sale at that price holds 511 blocks of $500 (the last one partial), so the combined tax comes to about $2,197. That is an illustration of the arithmetic, and your own deed will turn on the actual consideration.

Michigan's State Real Estate Transfer Tax Act, in MCL 207.526, lists transfers that owe no state tax. A deed that claims one must say so on its face.

  • A conveyance from a person to a child, stepchild, or adopted child, or to a grandchild.
  • A transfer made by foreclosure or by a deed given in lieu of foreclosure.
  • A court judgment or order that transfers the property, unless the court sets a specific money amount.
  • A deed that only confirms title already held, including a quitclaim that fixes a flaw.
  • A transfer where the price is under $100.

sections.h2: How do you get a deed into the Antrim County office?
sections.html:
The county encourages electronic recording through Simplifile or EPN, and it also accepts documents by mail, by courier and through a drop box. The drop box stands at the southeast corner of the building, and the register's page says it is checked periodically, so do not use it for a document with a closing deadline. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the original back.

Most sellers never touch this step. A title company or closing attorney prepares the deed, collects the transfer tax out of the proceeds and submits the file electronically. If you are handling a family transfer on your own, call the office first, because its staff can explain the filing steps even though they cannot draft the deed for you.

For a deed to be accepted it needs original signatures, an acknowledgment before a notary, the preparer's name and address, and a statement of the property's value or a filed valuation affidavit. Mistakes cost money to fix, so have a title professional read the draft.

sections.h2: Where do you pay property tax when you sell in Antrim County?
sections.html:
Current-year tax bills in Antrim County come from the local village or township, and the County Treasurer handles only prior years and delinquent tax. The treasurer's page says summer bills go out in July, village and township summer tax is due September 14, and township winter tax, billed in December, is due February 14. The bills cover the calendar year.

To pay an older year, the treasurer takes checks by mail at PO Box 544, Bellaire, MI 49615, card payments online or by phone at 231-533-6720, and drops at a secure box outside the public entrance. Cards carry a 2.95 percent fee with a $3.99 minimum. The office also lists the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services for possible help with tax costs.

When a house sells with tax unpaid, the title company asks the treasurer or the township for the balance and pays it at closing from the seller's proceeds. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure for the parcel before you list, so nothing surprises you on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What should an Antrim County seller know about the county itself?
sections.html:
Antrim County covers 602 square miles in northwest lower Michigan, and 126 of those are water. It is the home of Torch Lake, described on the county's Wikipedia entry as the deepest and second-largest inland lake in Michigan, and the Chain of Lakes sits mostly inside its borders. Grand Traverse Bay forms its western edge, and the county seat is Bellaire.

The incorporated places are the villages of Bellaire, Central Lake, Elk Rapids, Ellsworth and Mancelona. Census-designated places include Alba, Alden, Eastport and Lakes of the North. A lakefront parcel in Elk Rapids and a wooded lot near Mancelona can sell very differently, so ask for local comparables rather than a countywide number.

  • Estimated population in 2025: 24,698, up 5.4 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 86.4 percent, with 11,100 households.
  • Median household income: $72,054 (2020 to 2024 dollars).
  • Share of residents aged 65 and over: 30.7 percent.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 105.

Homes here are often seasonal or inherited, and a house that sat empty through winters can need roof, plumbing or septic work before a traditional buyer will close. A buyer who purchases as-is removes that repair list from the sale, which is the reason some owners choose a cash sale. You can request an offer at the top of the page.

faqs.q: How much does the Antrim County Register of Deeds charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $30.00 per document, with no extra fee for page count. Another $3.00 is added for each additional instrument that a single document assigns or discharges, and the $5.00 tax certificate from the treasurer applies to warranty deeds and land contracts.

faqs.q: Does Antrim County accept deeds recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The register's page encourages recording through Simplifile or EPN, and it still takes paper by mail, courier or the drop box at the southeast corner of the building. A title company usually handles the electronic filing for a sale.

faqs.q: Who collects current property tax in Antrim County?
faqs.a: The local village or township collects current-year tax, and the County Treasurer takes over for prior years and delinquent amounts. Summer bills go out in July with a September 14 due date to the township or village, and winter township tax is due February 14.

faqs.q: Can staff at the Antrim register's office help me write a deed?
faqs.a: They can explain what the office needs, but they cannot give legal advice or draft the document. For a family transfer or an estate sale, ask a title company or an attorney to prepare the deed, then call the office with filing questions.

faqs.q: Is transfer tax owed when a parent deeds a house to a child in Antrim County?
faqs.a: State transfer tax does not apply to a conveyance from an individual to a child, stepchild, adopted child or grandchild, under MCL 207.526. The deed has to state the exemption on its face, and the county portion has its own exemption language, so confirm the wording with the register's office before you sign.
